Craster

A tiny fishing village on the Northumberland coast, known for its harbour, smoked kippers and spectacular walks along the cliffs.

THE LOWDOWN

Why visit Craster?

Craster is one of Northumberland's most atmospheric coastal villages. The harbour sits at the heart of the village, with fishing boats coming and going and the distinctive smell of traditional kippers drifting through the air. From here, the coastline opens into some of the county's finest walking country, including the route to Dunstanburgh Castle.

HIGHLIGHTS

Things to see & do

Craster Harbour

Explore the working harbour and watch fishing boats coming and going from this atmospheric corner of the Northumberland coast.

Dunstanburgh Castle

Follow the spectacular coastal path from Craster towards the dramatic ruins of Dunstanburgh Castle.

The Coastal Walk

Walk along the cliffs and beaches around Craster for some of the finest scenery on Northumberland's Heritage Coast.

GOOD TO KNOW

Before you go

GETTING THERE

Craster is around 15 minutes from Alnwick by car. The village is reached by a narrow road from the A1 via Embleton.

BEST TIME TO VISIT

Spring through early autumn is ideal for coastal walks, although Craster has plenty of character throughout the year.

PARKING

A pay-and-display car park is available at the edge of the village. Parking can become busy during weekends and summer.
